conditions.required_condition_1: For isolated or recycled neutron stars at the beginning of the simulated spin-down phase, with period measured in seconds and no glitch-induced period jump at the initial epoch.

entries.selection_rationale: Use the literature-reported approximately 0.5 s birth period as the common pre-evolution baseline for isolated and recycled comparison tracks.

source.title: Birth and Evolution of Isolated Radio Pulsars

conditions.required_condition_1: For dipole torque models with approximately aligned magnetic and rotational axes represented by an angle in radians; treated as the starting value before inclination decay.

entries.selection_rationale: Adopt a 45 degree baseline inclination so the dipole torque is active without assuming either perfect alignment or orthogonality.

conditions.required_condition_1: For isolated neutron stars with approximately dipolar surface fields inferred from timing data, expressed in tesla; not intended for magnetar-like or strongly multipolar fields.

evidence_locator.quoted_text: typical values of 10 12 G and 107 yr for the normal pulsars

entries.selection_rationale: Use the review-reported 10^12 G normal-pulsar field, converted to 10^8 T, to represent the isolated-pulsar baseline.

conditions.required_condition_1: For the chosen effective spin-down law with magnetic field in tesla and period in seconds, assuming fixed stellar geometry and no unresolved internal braking physics.

entries.selection_rationale: Choose the effective coefficient so a 10^8 T, 0.5 s, 45 degree pulsar has an order-10^-15 period derivative; unresolved radius, inertia, and electromagnetic constants remain absorbed in this proxy.

conditions.required_condition_1: For pulsars with magnetospheric wind torque included as a multiplicative enhancement of the dipole term; scenario switches may disable the wind contribution.

entries.selection_rationale: Use a modest ten-percent wind-torque contribution as a sensitivity baseline while preserving dipole braking as the dominant isolated mechanism.

conditions.required_condition_1: For isolated pulsars modeled with smooth inclination decay, expressed in seconds, excluding glitches and abrupt magnetospheric state changes.

entries.selection_rationale: Use the review-reported order-10^7 yr inclination-evolution timescale converted to seconds.

conditions.required_condition_1: For recycled pulsars in a steady disk-accretion phase, expressed in kilograms per second, ignoring transient outbursts and companion ablation.

entries.selection_rationale: No compatible scalar survived extraction; adopt 6.3e14 kg/s as an explicit sub-Eddington sensitivity baseline for steady recycling rather than as a measured rate.

conditions.required_condition_1: For the effective accretion law using accretion rate in kilograms per second and dimensionless period derivative; active only during the accretion phase.

entries.selection_rationale: Set the reduced spin-up coefficient to permit substantial but finite period reduction over a 10 Myr accretion interval; it is an effective torque proxy, not a microphysical constant.

conditions.required_condition_1: For binary recycling tracks represented by a finite accretion interval followed by isolated spin-down, expressed in seconds.

entries.selection_rationale: Adopt a 10 Myr active recycling interval so the 100 Myr run retains a distinct post-accretion spin-down phase.

conditions.required_condition_1: Numerical endpoint for population synthesis tracks; not a physical observable unless tied to survey selection or evolutionary assumptions.

evidence_locator.quoted_text: over the lifetime of the pulsars as radio sources ( ∼ 100 Myr)

entries.selection_rationale: Use the reported approximately 100 Myr radio-pulsar lifetime as the integration horizon.

source.title: Birth and Evolution of Isolated Radio Pulsars

conditions.required_condition_1: Survey-dependent detection boundary for timing observations; used as a stopping condition rather than a physical spin-down parameter.

entries.selection_rationale: Use 10^-22 s/s as a permissive numerical detectability floor to stop effectively inactive tracks without truncating ordinary pulsar evolution.

conditions.required_condition_1: Numerical control for population synthesis; chosen for computational budget and statistical resolution rather than physical measurement.

entries.selection_rationale: Use 5000 tracks as a computationally bounded first-pass population sample large enough for stable distribution summaries.
